outcome: small for gestational age at birth
cohort: 15,760 pregnancies with obesity (early pregnancy BMI before 14 weeks' gestation ≥30 kg/m(2)) among singleton pregnancies that delivered between January 1, 2008, and December 31, 2015, from the Stockholm-Gotland Perinatal Cohort study
finding: Gestational weight gain below the lower limit of the Institute of Medicine (IOM) recommendation (5 kg at term) or weight loss was not associated with increased risk of adverse outcomes in pregnancies with class 1 or 2 obesity, but was associated with reduced risk in class 3 obesity.
mod_finding: Gestational weight gain below the lower limit of the IOM recommendation or weight loss was not associated with an increased risk of unplanned cesarean delivery in women with class 1 or 2 obesity, and was associated with a reduced risk in those with class 3 obesity.
